A_target.statement:
Let a [[Definition:Prefix Code|prefix-free]] binary code have codeword lengths $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_m$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^m 2^{-\ell_i} \le 1$
Conversely, any lengths satisfying this inequality are the lengths of some prefix-free binary code.

B_source.statement: In the complete binary tree of depth $L$, a node at depth $\ell$ has $2^{L - \ell}$ descendant leaves, and nodes none of which is an ancestor of another have disjoint sets of descendant leaves.

substitutions.prefix-freeness: no codeword node is an ancestor of another

derived.disjoint leaf sets: the Kraft sum is at most 1

object_map.reformulation: Represent codewords as nodes of a binary tree and count the leaves below them.

validity_conditions: L is taken as the maximum codeword length.
For the converse, assigning codewords in order of increasing length keeps a free node available.
proof_plan:
Identify binary words with nodes of the infinite binary tree; a word is a prefix of another {{iff}} its node is an ancestor.
Let $L = \max_i \ell_i$.
By the source result, the codeword of length $\ell_i$ has $2^{L - \ell_i}$ descendant leaves at depth $L$, and these sets are disjoint.

Conversely, sort $\ell_1 \le \cdots \le \ell_m$ and give each the leftmost free node of its depth; before step $j$ the used leaves number $\displaystyle \sum_{i < j} 2^{L - \ell_i} < 2^L$, so a free node exists.
{{qed}}
